meta.title: Part III consolidated experimental warrant source (TTT/neural-memory decode = memory-centric)
meta.thesis: D4 workload-split pair thesis: decode/serving state management is a memory-centric opportunity (per-token RMW of the whole fast-weight state; unshared, write-heavy, not content-addressable -> qualitatively unlike append-once/read-many KV cache); training/prefill is the accelerator regime (chunk C is the roofline x-axis).
meta.grade: EXPLORATION-GRADE. Load-bearing claims = ratios, crossover positions, tier orderings, bound classifications. Absolute wall-clock deferred to in-house A100 runbook (Part III-a).
meta.anchor_config: neural-mem-1.3B (d=2048, m=16, L=24, GQA-8 kv_dim=1024, bf16)

caveat_tag_glossary.REL: exploration-grade / RELATIVE: hatir + hat-schema twins are pre-silicon analytic cost models (repo self-declares ranking+crossover, not silicon-accurate absolutes); only ratios and crossover POSITIONS are promoted to text.
caveat_tag_glossary.NO-WALLCLOCK: the 6 source papers do NOT publish H100 wall-clock decode; absolute us/token & mJ/token are roofline lower bounds, externally unverifiable, deferred to the in-house A100 runbook (Part III-a).
caveat_tag_glossary.PER-KERNEL: per-kernel roofline only: no kernel-launch / scheduling / decode tail-effect overheads; per-token latency is a lower bound.
caveat_tag_glossary.NOVEL-SIM-FALSE: novel twins (novel-swscratchpad-npu, novel-pim-cim) are provenance=analytical -> verify committee marks simulation_ready=False / PPA-abstain; PIM & scratchpad results are DIRECTIONAL DSE only, never a shipping-device claim.
caveat_tag_glossary.CPU-SHAPE: CPU micro-bench validates the SHAPE (how the quantity scales) and the memory<->compute crossover ONLY; it does NOT transport to H100 absolutes (host ridge ~34 FLOP/B sits ~9x below the H100 twin ridge 295 FLOP/B; host cache cliff ~100x off the H100 on/off-die ridge).
caveat_tag_glossary.M-ASSUMED: state multipliers m (2-layer MLP=8d^2, +momentum=16d^2) and (d,L) per param scale are canonical transformer shapes from published architecture descriptions, not released decode traces.
caveat_tag_glossary.RESIDENCY-3RD-CLASS: residency.py excludes PERSISTENT tensors from the transient set; TTT state is a 3rd class (persistent BUT mutated every token) so it is tagged activation-class to force the spill sim; eviction-policy precision not claimed.

source_experiments.E3-analytical: closed-form cost model + crossover calculator (S*, C*, B_max) over 6 papers x 5 model scales
source_experiments.E1.1-decode-baseline: hatir decode-step baseline on DGX-H100 twin: traffic/time/energy/bound
source_experiments.E1.2-state-placement: hatir state-placement DSE: HBM vs SRAM vs scratchpad vs PIM, residency crossover, spill
source_experiments.E1.3-kv-vs-ttt: hatir KV-vs-TTT contrast: S* crossover, B_max, read/write traffic decomposition
source_experiments.E1.4-frequency-tiers: hatir frequency-tiered placement: update cadence -> memory-hierarchy tier admissibility
source_experiments.E1.5-kvmgr-gap: hat-kv-manager semantic-gap analysis: prefix-reuse=0, stale accretion, unpriced dirty writeback
source_experiments.E2.1-chunk-intensity: CPU numpy micro-bench: AI(C) curve shape + memory->compute crossover on host roofline
source_experiments.E2.2-rmw-cliff: CPU numpy micro-bench: RMW bandwidth cliff at the on-die/off-die (L3->DRAM) capacity boundary

claim1_decode_is_memorybound_rmw.supports: pair thesis, decode half: 'decode = per-token RMW of the entire fast-weight state'
claim1_decode_is_memorybound_rmw.anchor: neural-mem-1.3B (d=2048, m=16, L=24, GQA-8 kv_dim=1024, bf16)

rmw_GB_per_token.note: read m*d^2 + write m*d^2 over L layers; 3-way agree (E1.1=6.4425, E3=6.442, E1.3=6.4425)

decode_ms_per_token.note: state-movement lower bound at HBM3 3.35 TB/s

arith_intensity_flopB.note: << ridge 295 FLOP/B => deterministically memory-bound (E1.1 gemv-inclusive AI=2.25 also << ridge)

memory_over_gemv_compute_ratio.note: state RMW dominates the GEMV compute of a decode step by ~394x => step cost IS the state traffic

scaling_rmw_GB_per_token.note: RMW traffic grows with model width d^2*m*L; independent of context S (the KV contrast).

claim2_kv_vs_ttt_crossover.supports: pair thesis core: why decode-state management is a NEW memory opportunity, not KV cache
claim2_kv_vs_ttt_crossover.anchor: neural-mem-1.3B (d=2048, m=16, L=24, GQA-8 kv_dim=1024, bf16)

kv.note: KV write (append) is 0.003% of read => append-once/read-many

ttt.note: TTT write == read (equal halves) => symmetric RMW, always dirty

S_star_read_tokens.note: context at which KV read traffic == TTT read half; below S* KV is cheaper, above S* TTT is cheaper. E3 closed form 65536, hatir 65471 (agree).

S_star_rmw_tokens.note: context at which KV read == full TTT RMW (read+write); the honest upper crossover.

S_star_scaling.MHA_collapses_S_star: kv_dim=d shrinks S* linearly (see E3 sweeps.S_star.kv_dim_d_MHA)

kv_latency_grows_with_context.note: dense-attention KV decode per-token latency RISES with context (read-many wall); TTT per-token latency is context-INDEPENDENT (constant RMW).

claim3_batch_scaling_Bmax.supports: pair thesis: serving economics of decode-state (BW binds, opposite of capacity-bound KV cache)

batching_feasibility_gloss.note: batching stays FEASIBLE via grouped-GEMM/BMM over the batch axis (per user analysis + ch24 proposal G); what dies is shared-weight AMORTIZATION: each request carries its own fast-weight state so arithmetic intensity is independent of B, and BW closes the batch early at B_max. Read the B_max limit as 'batch amortization vanishes', NOT 'batching is mathematically impossible'.

binding_resource.note: at every model scale B_max is BW-bound at 10ms, far below the HBM-capacity batch => opposite of KV cache which is capacity-bound

ondie_holds_one_seq.note: on-die L2 (50MB) cannot hold even ONE sequence's whole-model state at any scale => TTT state cannot be pinned on-die whole-model; residency must be per-layer/streamed (motivates E1.2)

claim4_state_placement_dse.supports: memory-centric opportunity: TTT state size is context-INDEPENDENT (fixed by d,m,L) so on-chip residency is a designable knob, unlike context-growing KV

device_ranking_134MB_layer_RMW.note: flat single-tier device twins so traffic (2*S) is byte-comparable; state=134MB/layer (d=2048,m=16)

energy_win_x.note: 268MB scratchpad vs HBM3 for a resident 134MB RMW

whole_model_fits_268MB_scratchpad.note: every config >=340M overruns and spills per token => at scale placement is per-layer/streamed, not pinned whole-model

pim_for_write_heavy_epilogue.note: PIM wins energy on the write-heavy elementwise epilogue while its intensity stays low
pim_for_write_heavy_epilogue.note2: PIM latency only bites past ~3 MAC/elem (compute-bound epilogue); at rank-1-ish 1 MAC/elem it is 1.74x energy AND 0.7x time

claim5_frequency_tiered_placement.supports: Nested-Learning(HOPE)/Sleep update-cadence continuum translates DIRECTLY to a tier assignment; sub-per-token access cadence is what lets a write-heavy RMW state legally drop to DDR/CXL
claim5_frequency_tiered_placement.anchor: neural-mem-1.3B, per-token critical-path budget t_tok = 961.6 us (all-layer RMW on HBM3)

gating_rule.value: resident copy gated by max(read-cadence, write-cadence) i.e. the FASTER access

fast-weights (read+write every token).reason: read-gated to fastest admissible resident tier

CMS-chunk (read/token, write/64 tokens).reason: read cadence pins it hot despite chunked write

CMS-mid (read+write /4096 tokens).reason: down-sampled cadence => cheapest tier still admissible

per_layer_scratchpad_energy_win_x.note: per-LAYER fast-weight block (67MB) fits the 268MB scratchpad: 7.4x lower energy than HBM3; all-layer does NOT fit

claim6_kvmanager_semantic_gap.supports: software-stack half of the pair thesis: existing KV-cache manager cannot manage TTT state

ttt.note: content-addressed reuse (the manager's #1 value) is structurally ZERO for RMW state: content changes every token, no block hash recurs

G2_stale_accretion_blowup_x.note: append-only place() with no in-place update accretes T=256 stale versions => 256x the true 1-state working set

mgr_charged_writeback.note: _evict_from() del-drops dirty state for free (clean/recomputable assumption)

owed_writeback_energy_uJ.note: dirty TTT state owes a full writeback the manager prices as ZERO

missing_api_for_ttt_state.note: event types a TTT-state manager needs that KVCacheManager lacks

claim7_chunk_is_roofline_axis.supports: pair thesis, training/prefill half: growing chunk C moves the SAME algorithm from memory-bound (C=1 sequential decode regime) to compute-bound (accelerator regime)

AI_at_C1_sequential_flopB.note: C=1 per-token rank-1 RMW (== TTT decode regime) sits at AI~1 => deep memory-bound plateau, measured only ~12% of host roofline

C_star_measured_discrete.note: measured memory->compute crossover on host (all d in {512,1024,2048}); continuous ~23-24

C_star_h100_closedform.note: on the H100 twin ridge (295 FLOP/B) C* is ~306-430 depending on d; the CPU confirms the SHAPE, not this value

claim8_rmw_bandwidth_cliff.supports: state placement: an in-cache (on-die) RMW is cheap; overrun the capacity boundary and effective BW collapses -- the local analogue of the E1.2 scratchpad fit->spill cliff

l3_to_dram_cliff_x.note: on-die vs off-die RMW bandwidth ratio at the L3 capacity boundary (the robust, overhead-free headline)

readonly_over_rmw_at_dram.note: RMW moves 2x the bytes/element of a read => ~half the effective element throughput at saturated DRAM; quantifies the write-back tax that append-once KV avoids

cross_validation.note: closed-form (E3), hatir tool (E1.1/E1.3), and plan hand-calc agree on the anchor to <1%
cross_validation.anchor: neural-mem-1.3B (d=2048, m=16, L=24, GQA-8 kv_dim=1024, bf16)

C_star_shape.note: same curve shape, ridge-dependent value; CPU ridge 9x below H100

carry_forward_to_A100_runbook: Absolute per-token decode wall-clock (ms/token, tokens/s) at every model scale: the papers publish none, so E1.1/E3 give only a roofline lower bound. Measure real decode latency + achieved HBM BW on A100.
Achieved-vs-roofline efficiency of the RMW step (kernel-launch, scheduling, tail): E1.1 is per-kernel only.
Real energy/token: HBM twin uses a symmetric 7 pJ/B; measure actual r/w-asymmetric DRAM energy on A100.
S* validation with a REAL KV read kernel + a REAL TTT state kernel head-to-head (E1.3 uses roofline halves).
Novel-twin (scratchpad/PIM) numbers stay DIRECTIONAL until silicon: E1.2/E1.4 scratchpad wins are not device claims.
B_max under a full serving stack (weights + activations + KV co-resident): E3 B_max_cap is an upper bound.
